question:
Match the concepts in column A with their respective descriptions in column B.
Column A Column B
a. Gross national product 1. Annual income received by the individual's
production in a given period
b. Net national product 2. After the tax of personal income
c. Personal income 3. Money value of the national output
d. Disposable personal income 4. Net production of goods services during the year

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: a-2, b-1, c-3, d-4
a-3, b-1, c-2, d-4
a-3, b-4, c-1, d-2
a-4, b-3, c-2, d-1
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is a-3, b-4, c-1, d-2

Explanation:
This question involves matching national income concepts with their descriptions. Gross National Product (GNP) is the money value of national output (3), while Net National Product (NNP) is the net production of goods and services during the year (4). Personal Income is the annual income received by an individual from production in a given period (1), and Disposable Personal Income is personal income after taxes (2). These concepts are part of national income accounting and are crucial for measuring economic performance.

Extra Facts:
National Income is the total value of all final goods and services produced by a country in a year. GNP includes net income from abroad, while NNP is derived by subtracting depreciation from GNP. Personal Income includes all types of income, whereas Disposable Income is post-tax income available for spending or saving. These concepts play a vital role in economic planning and policy-making.

question:
Which of the following organizations of the Government of India has been reporting the GDP at factor cost and at market prices?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Reserve Bank of India
National Sample Survey Organisation
National Statistics Office
NITI Aayog
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Statistics Office (NSO)

Explanation:
The National Statistics Office (NSO) is the primary agency of the Government of India responsible for calculating and reporting GDP at Factor Cost and GDP at Market Prices. It was formed by merging the Central Statistics Office (CSO) and the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO). GDP at Factor Cost measures the cost of production factors (labor, capital, land), while GDP at Market Prices includes indirect taxes and subsidies. NSO's data plays a crucial role in economic policymaking and analysis.

Extra Facts:
The key difference between GDP at Factor Cost and GDP at Market Prices is 'Net Indirect Taxes (Indirect Taxes - Subsidies)'. India's GDP is calculated based on a Base Year (currently 2011-12), which is periodically updated. While RBI and NITI Aayog use economic data, the official GDP calculation is done by NSO.

Explanation:
राष्ट्रीय सांख्यिकी कार्यालय (NSO) भारत सरकार की प्रमुख संस्था है जो 'कारक लागत पर सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP at Factor Cost)' और 'बाजार मूल्य पर सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP at Market Prices)' की गणना और प्रकाशन करती है। यह संस्था केंद्रीय सांख्यिकी कार्यालय (CSO) और राष्ट्रीय नमूना सर्वेक्षण कार्यालय (NSSO) के विलय से बनी है। GDP की गणना में 'कारक लागत' उत्पादन के कारकों (श्रम, पूंजी, भूमि) की लागत को दर्शाती है, जबकि 'बाजार मूल्य' में अप्रत्यक्ष कर और सब्सिडी शामिल होती है। NSO द्वारा जारी आंकड़े आर्थिक नीति निर्माण और विश्लेषण में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं।

Extra Facts:
GDP at Factor Cost और GDP at Market Prices के बीच मुख्य अंतर 'नेट अप्रत्यक्ष कर (Indirect Taxes - Subsidies)' है। भारत में GDP का आकलन आधार वर्ष (Base Year) के अनुसार किया जाता है, जिसे समय-समय पर अपडेट किया जाता है (वर्तमान में 2011-12 आधार वर्ष है)। NSO के अलावा, भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (RBI) और नीति आयोग (NITI Aayog) भी आर्थिक डेटा का उपयोग करते हैं, लेकिन GDP की आधिकारिक गणना NSO द्वारा ही की जाती है।

question:
If the saving function is S= - 30 + 0.3Y, what will be the value of MPC (marginal propensity to consume)?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: 0.9
0
0.3
0.7
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 0.7

Explanation:
The saving function is given as S = -30 + 0.3Y. The sum of the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) and the marginal propensity to save (MPS) is always equal to 1, i.e., MPC + MPS = 1. Here, MPS is the coefficient of Y in the saving function, which is 0.3. Therefore, MPC = 1 - MPS = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7. This is a key part of 'Keynesian theory' in economics, which explains the relationship between income and consumption.

Extra Facts:
According to Keynesian theory, MPC and MPS always lie between 0 and 1. MPC is calculated as the change in consumption divided by the change in income (MPC = ΔC/ΔY). It is crucial in economic models because it indicates how much of an increase in income will be spent on consumption. Economies with a high MPC experience a greater impact of income growth on consumption, which boosts aggregate demand.

question_hi:
यदि बचत फलन S= - 30 + 0.3Y, है, तो MPC (सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति) का मान क्या होगा?

[RRC GROUP D]
options_hi: 0.9
0
0.3
0.7
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 0.7

Explanation:
बचत फलन (S) = -30 + 0.3Y दिया गया है। सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति (MPC) और सीमांत बचत प्रवृत्ति (MPS) का योग हमेशा 1 के बराबर होता है, अर्थात MPC + MPS = 1। यहाँ, MPS (सीमांत बचत प्रवृत्ति) बचत फलन में Y का गुणांक है, जो 0.3 है। इसलिए, MPC = 1 - MPS = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7 होगा। यह अर्थशास्त्र में 'Keynesian सिद्धांत' का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है, जो आय और उपभोग के बीच संबंध को दर्शाता है।

Extra Facts:
Keynesian सिद्धांत के अनुसार, MPC और MPS हमेशा 0 और 1 के बीच होते हैं। MPC उपभोग में परिवर्तन को आय में परिवर्तन से विभाजित करके निकाला जाता है (MPC = ΔC/ΔY)। यह आर्थिक मॉडल में महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह बताता है कि आय में वृद्धि का कितना हिस्सा उपभोग पर खर्च किया जाएगा। उच्च MPC वाली अर्थव्यवस्थाओं में, आय में वृद्धि का अधिक प्रभाव उपभोग पर पड़ता है, जो समग्र मांग को बढ़ाता है।

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I.Only marketed goods are considered while estimating Gross Domestic Product
II. The work done by a woman at her home is outside the purview of Gross Domestic Product.
III. In estimating GDP, only final goods and services are considered.

[SSC CGL 2021]
options:
Only II and III

I, II and III

Only I and III

Only II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only II and III

Explanation:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year. Statement I is incorrect because GDP includes not only marketed goods but also non-marketed activities (e.g., government services). Statement II is correct as unpaid domestic work (e.g., a woman’s household chores) is excluded from GDP since it lacks market valuation. Statement III is correctdouble-counting of intermediate goods.

Extra Facts:
GDP is calculated via three methods: Production, Income, and Expenditure approaches. GDP excludes illegal activities (e.g., black market). In India, GDP is estimated by the Central Statistics Office (CSO). An alternative measure is GNP (Gross National Product), which accounts for production by a country's citizens domestically and abroad.

question_hi:

II. एक महिला द्वारा अपने घर पर किया गया कार्य सकल घरेलू उत्पाद के दायरे से बाहर है।

[SSC CGL 2021]
options_hi:
केवल II और III

I, II और III

केवल I और III

केवल II
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है केवल II और III

Explanation:
सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) एक वर्ष में एक देश की सीमा के भीतर उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का बाजार मूल्य है। कथन I गलत है क्योंकि GDP में केवल विपणन की गई वस्तुओं को ही नहीं, बल्कि गैर-विपणन गतिविधियों (जैसे सरकारी सेवाएं) को भी शामिल किया जाता है। कथन II सही है क्योंकि घरेलू कार्य (जैसे महिलाओं द्वारा घर पर किया गया काम) GDP में शामिल नहीं होता क्योंकि इसका बाजार में कोई मूल्य नहीं होता। कथन III सही है क्योंकि GDP की गणना में केवल अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं को ही शामिल किया जाता है, मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं को नहीं, ताकि दोहरी गणना से बचा जा सके।

Extra Facts:

question:
Consider the given consumption function of country X and answer the following question.
C = 100 + 0.8Y
What is the value of autonomous consumption (A) and marginal propensity to consume (MPC) in the given equation?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: A = 0.8, MPC = 100
A = 100, MPC = 80
A = 80, MPC = 0.10
A = 100, MPC = 0.8
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A = 100, MPC = 0.8

Explanation:
In the given consumption function C = 100 + 0.8Y, 100 represents autonomous consumption (A), which is independent of income (Y). It is the consumption that occurs even when income is zero. 0.8 represents the marginal propensity to consume (MPC), which measures the increase in consumption for every unit increase in income. MPC always lies between 0 and 1. Here, MPC = 0.8 implies that for every 1 rupee increase in income, consumption will increase by 0.8 rupees.

Extra Facts:
Autonomous consumption (A) and marginal propensity to consume (MPC) are key concepts in Keynesian consumption function. MPC is calculated as ΔC/ΔY, where ΔC is change in consumption and ΔY is change in income. The value of MPC is crucial in understanding the impact of fiscal policies like taxation and government spending. Economies with higher MPC experience greater multiplier effects from fiscal policies.

देश x के दिए गए उपभोग फलन पर विचार करें और निम्नलिखित प्रश्न का उत्तर दें। C = 100 + 0.8Y
दिए गए समीकरण में स्वायत्त उपभोग (A) और सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति (MPC) का मूल्य क्या है?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options_hi: A = 0.8, MPC = 100
A = 100, MPC = 80
A = 80, MPC = 0.10
A = 100, MPC = 0.8
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है A = 100, MPC = 0.8

Explanation:
दिए गए उपभोग फलन C = 100 + 0.8Y में, 100 स्वायत्त उपभोग (A) को दर्शाता है, जो आय (Y) से स्वतंत्र होता है। यह वह उपभोग है जो आय के शून्य होने पर भी होता है। 0.8 सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति (MPC) को दर्शाता है, जो आय में होने वाली प्रति इकाई वृद्धि पर उपभोग में होने वाली वृद्धि को मापता है। MPC हमेशा 0 और 1 के बीच होता है। यहां, MPC = 0.8 का अर्थ है कि आय में प्रत्येक 1 रुपये की वृद्धि पर उपभोग में 0.8 रुपये की वृद्धि होगी।

Extra Facts:
स्वायत्त उपभोग (A) और सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति (MPC) की अवधारणाएं केन्ज़ के उपभोग फलन का हिस्सा हैं। MPC की गणना ΔC/ΔY के रूप में की जाती है, जहां ΔC उपभोग में परिवर्तन और ΔY आय में परिवर्तन है। MPC का मूल्य आर्थिक नीतियों, जैसे कर और सरकारी खर्च, के प्रभाव को समझने में महत्वपूर्ण है। उच्च MPC वाले अर्थव्यवस्थाओं में राजकोषीय नीतियों का प्रभाव अधिक होता है।

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct with respect to income or output?
i. Income or output are flows.
ii. Income or output are stocks.
iii. Income or output can be defined over a period.

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Only i and iii
Only ii and iii
Only i
Only i and ii
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only i and iii

Explanation:
Income or output are flows because they are measured over a period of time, such as Gross Domestic Product (GDP), which is the value of goods and services produced in a year. Stock variables like capital or wealth are measured at a particular point in time, while flow variables are measured over time. Thus, statement i is correct and statement ii is incorrect. Statement iii is also correct because income or output is always defined over a period (e.g., monthly, quarterly, annually).

Extra Facts:
Flow and stock are fundamental concepts in economics. Flow variables change over time and are measured 'per unit of time' (e.g., income, investment). Stock variables are measured at a specific point in time (e.g., wealth, capital). Indicators like GDP, GNP, and national income are flows, while assets, debt, and capital stock are stocks. This distinction is crucial in macroeconomic analysis.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ What is the difference between flow and stock? → Flow is measured over time, stock at a point in time
☛ What is GDP? → Value of final goods and services produced in a year
☛ What type of variable is national income? → Flow variable
☛ What type of variable is capital? → Stock variable
☛ What type of variable is investment? → Flow variable

आय या निर्गत के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?

केवल ii और iii
केवल i

हल: सही उत्तर है केवल i और iii

Explanation:
आय या निर्गत प्रवाह हैं क्योंकि ये समय की एक अवधि में मापे जाते हैं, जैसे सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) जो एक वर्ष में उत्पादित वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का मूल्य है। स्टॉक चर जैसे पूंजी या धन एक विशेष समय पर मापे जाते हैं, जबकि प्रवाह चर समय के साथ मापे जाते हैं। इसलिए, कथन i सही है और कथन ii गलत है। कथन iii भी सही है क्योंकि आय या निर्गत को हमेशा एक अवधि (जैसे मासिक, त्रैमासिक, वार्षिक) के लिए परिभाषित किया जाता है।

प्रवाह और स्टॉक अर्थशास्त्र के मूलभूत अवधारणाएं हैं। प्रवाह चर समय के साथ बदलते हैं और उन्हें 'प्रति इकाई समय' में मापा जाता है (जैसे आय, निवेश)। स्टॉक चर किसी विशेष समय बिंदु पर मापे जाते हैं (जैसे धन, पूंजी)। GDP, GNP, राष्ट्रीय आय जैसे संकेतक प्रवाह हैं, जबकि संपत्ति, ऋण, पूंजी स्टॉक स्टॉक हैं। यह अंतर मैक्रोइकॉनॉमिक विश्लेषण में महत्वपूर्ण है।

question:
Depreciation is an annual allowance for the wear and tear of ______.

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: finished goods
capital goods
work in progress
land
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is capital goods

Explanation:
Depreciation is an annual allowance provided for the wear and tear of capital goods (such as machinery, equipment, buildings, etc.) due to usage, obsolescence, or passage of time. It is a non-cash expense that reduces the value of an asset on the balance sheet and is recorded as an expense in the profit & loss account. The purpose of depreciation is to allocate the cost of an asset over its useful life.

Extra Facts:
- The two main methods of calculating depreciation are the Straight Line Method and the Written Down Value Method.
- Land does not depreciate as its value typically appreciates over time.
- Finished goods and work in progress are part of inventory and are not subject to depreciation.

☛ What are the two methods of depreciation? → Straight Line and Written Down Value

☛ What is depreciation? → Reduction in value of capital assets
☛ Example of a non-cash expense? → Depreciation
question_hi:
मूल्यह्रास ______ के क्षति के कारण एक वार्षिक भत्ता है।

[SSC CGL 2019]
options_hi: तैयार माल
पूंजीगत सामान
कार्य प्रगति पर है
भूमि
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है पूंजीगत सामान

Explanation:
मूल्यह्रास (Depreciation) एक वार्षिक भत्ता है जो पूंजीगत सामान (जैसे मशीनरी, उपकरण, भवन आदि) के उपयोग, घिसावट और समय के साथ मूल्य में कमी के कारण दिया जाता है। यह एक गैर-नकद व्यय है जो कंपनी की बैलेंस शीट में संपत्ति के मूल्य को कम करता है और लाभ-हानि खाते में व्यय के रूप में दर्ज किया जाता है। मूल्यह्रास का उद्देश्य संपत्ति के मूल्य को उसके उपयोगी जीवनकाल में आनुपातिक रूप से आवंटित करना है।

Extra Facts:

question:
Which of these statements is correct?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: The economic wealth of a country does not necessarily depend on the possession of resources.
Countries endowed with natural resources are naturally the richest countries.
The national income of a country is the total of all its resources.
Whether resources are used in generating a flow of output and as a result, income and wealth, is immaterial.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The economic wealth of a country does not necessarily depend on the possession of resources.

Explanation:
A country's economic prosperity is not solely dependent on the availability of resources but also on their efficient utilization and management. For example, countries like Japan have limited natural resources but are economically prosperous due to technological expertise and human capital. Conversely, some resource-rich nations remain economically underdeveloped due to factors like poor resource management or corruption. Thus, while resources are important, their optimal use and governance are more critical for economic success.

Extra Facts:
In economics, resources are categorized into natural resources (e.g., minerals, water, forests) and man-made resources (e.g., technology, capital, human skills). Balanced utilization of both is vital for development. The Resource Curse theory highlights how excessive natural resources can hinder growth by promoting corruption and inequality. Countries like Norway, however, avoid this curse through transparent governance and investment in human capital.

☛ Key factor for economic prosperity? → Efficient resource utilization
☛ Why is Japan economically successful? → Technological advancement and human capital

प्राकृतिक संसाधनों से संपन्न देश स्वाभाविक रूप से सबसे धनी देश होते हैं।

क्या उपयोग किए जा रहे संसाधन जिनसे उत्पादन का प्रवाह उत्पन्न हो तथा आय और संपत्ति का सृजन हो, अनावश्यक हैं।
solution_hi:

Explanation:
किसी देश की आर्थिक संपन्नता केवल संसाधनों की उपलब्धता पर निर्भर नहीं करती है, बल्कि उन संसाधनों के कुशल उपयोग और प्रबंधन पर भी निर्भर करती है। उदाहरण के लिए, जापान जैसे देशों में प्राकृतिक संसाधन कम हैं, लेकिन वे तकनीकी कुशलता और मानव संसाधन के कारण आर्थिक रूप से संपन्न हैं। इसके विपरीत, कुछ देश प्राकृतिक संसाधनों से भरपूर होते हुए भी आर्थिक रूप से पिछड़े हैं। यह संसाधनों के अल्प-उपयोग या भ्रष्टाचार जैसे कारकों के कारण हो सकता है। अतः, संसाधनों का होना महत्वपूर्ण है, लेकिन उनका सही उपयोग और प्रबंधन अधिक महत्वपूर्ण है।

Extra Facts:
संसाधनों का अर्थशास्त्र में, संसाधनों को दो श्रेणियों में बांटा जाता है: प्राकृतिक संसाधन (जैसे खनिज, जल, वन) और मानव निर्मित संसाधन (जैसे तकनीक, पूंजी, मानव कौशल)। आर्थिक विकास के लिए दोनों का संतुलित उपयोग आवश्यक है। संसाधन अभिशाप (Resource Curse) एक महत्वपूर्ण अवधारणा है, जिसके अनुसार कुछ देशों में प्राकृतिक संसाधनों की अधिकता उनके आर्थिक विकास में बाधक बन जाती है, क्योंकि यह भ्रष्टाचार और असमानता को बढ़ावा देती है।

question:
Which of the following is NOT included in the national income?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Income received by a person as a donation
Income received by a household for the use of their entrepreneurial skill
Income received by a person for the use of his capital

Income received by a household for the use of their land
.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Income received by a person as a donation

Explanation:
National income includes only those incomes that are earned as a result of productive activities. Income received as a donation is a 'transfer payment', which is not associated with any production activity. Hence, it is not included in national income. Other options like income from entrepreneurial skills, capital, and land are factor incomes, which are part of national income.

Extra Facts:
National income is calculated using parameters like GDP, GNP, and NNP. Transfer payments (e.g., pensions, scholarships, donations) are excluded because they are not linked to current production activities. Factor incomes (wages, interest, profit, rent) are rewards for contributions to the production process and are thus included in national income.

question:
Why are the intermediate goods NOT included in the National Income ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Intermediate goods increases the income.
Intermediate goods decreases the income.
For the prevention of double accounting.
Intermediate goods are not reliable.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is For the prevention of double accounting.

Explanation:
Intermediate goods are not included in the calculation of National Income to avoid double counting. Intermediate goods are those used as raw materials in the production of other goods. If they are included in national income, their value would already be part of the final goods' value, leading to an incorrect total income estimation. For example, wheat used to make flour is an intermediate good. If both wheat and flour values are added, it would result in double counting. Hence, only final goods and services are included in national income to ensure accurate measurement.

Extra Facts:
National Income is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year. It is measured as GDP (Gross Domestic Product) or GNP (Gross National Product). The Value Added Method is used to prevent double counting, where only the value added at each production stage is summed up. This method accurately reflects the contribution of different sectors of the economy. Intermediate goods like raw materials, fuel, etc., are excluded to maintain the integrity of national income calculations.

☛ Which method is used to avoid double counting? → Value Added Method
☛ What is the full form of GDP? → Gross Domestic Product
☛ What does GNP include? → Income earned by citizens domestically and abroad
☛ What are final goods? → Goods ready for consumption or investment

question:
Which of the following is a correct statement?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: National Income is GNP at FC.
National Income is NDP at MP.
National Income is GDP at MP.
National Income is NNP at FC.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Income is NNP at FC.

Explanation:
The most accurate measure of National Income is Net National Product (NNP) at Factor Cost (FC). NNP accounts for depreciation, reflecting the net economic output of a nation. At Factor Cost, NNP adjusts for indirect taxes (subtracted) and subsidies (added), providing a clearer picture of real income. This measure is widely used in economic analysis because it better represents the actual income available to a nation after accounting for capital consumption and fiscal adjustments.

Extra Facts:
National Income can be measured using GDP, GNP, NDP, and NNP. GDP is the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year, while GNP includes net income from abroad. NNP deducts depreciation to show net production, crucial for long-term economic stability. NNP at Factor Cost is the most precise measure of real national income as it excludes indirect taxes and includes subsidies, reflecting true economic output.

☛ What are Indirect Taxes? → Taxes paid by consumers indirectly

question:
Which cost is considered for calculating the national income in India?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: Product cost
Factor cost
Market cost
Sunk cost
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Factor cost

Explanation:
In India, national income is calculated at 'Factor Cost'. Factor cost refers to the income calculated based on the remuneration paid to the factors of production (such as labor, capital, land, and enterprise). It adjusts for indirect taxes (like GST) and subsidies, providing an accurate measure of real income. 'Market Cost' includes indirect taxes, but factor cost is more appropriate for national income calculation as it reflects the actual income of the factors of production.

Extra Facts:
National Income measures the total economic activity of a country, including the value of all goods and services. It is measured using parameters like GDP (Gross Domestic Product), GNP (Gross National Product), and NNP (Net National Product). NNP at factor cost is referred to as national income. It helps in understanding the real state of the economy.

question:
Which of the following is true about transfer payments in relation to personal income?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: Transfer payments are included in personal income.
Transfer payments have no impact on personal income.
Transfer payments are included in personal income only for businesses
Transfer payments are excluded from personal income.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Transfer payments are included in personal income.

Explanation:
Transfer payments are payments made by the government or other entities without receiving any goods or services in return, such as pensions, unemployment benefits, scholarships, etc. These payments are included in personal income because they increase individuals' income. Personal income encompasses all types of income, whether earned through labor, capital, or transfer payments. Therefore, the statement that transfer payments are included in personal income is correct.

Extra Facts:
Personal Income represents all income earned by an individual or household during a specific period. It includes wages, interest, dividends, rent, and transfer payments. The purpose of transfer payments is to redistribute income and enhance social welfare. These payments are excluded from National Income as they are not linked to production activities, but they are included in personal income.

वैयक्तिक आय (Personal Income) एक व्यक्ति या परिवार द्वारा किसी विशेष समयावधि में अर्जित सभी आय को दर्शाती है। इसमें मजदूरी, ब्याज, लाभांश, किराया, और अंतरण भुगतान शामिल होते हैं। अंतरण भुगतान का उद्देश्य आय का पुनर्वितरण करना और सामाजिक कल्याण को बढ़ाना है। ये भुगतान राष्ट्रीय आय (National Income) में शामिल नहीं होते क्योंकि ये उत्पादन गतिविधियों से जुड़े नहीं होते, लेकिन वैयक्तिक आय में शामिल होते हैं।

question:
Which of the following is NOT included in inventory investment when calculating national income ?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Change in sales during the year
Change in stock of semi-finished goods
Change in stock of raw material
Change in stock of finished goods
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Change in sales during the year

Explanation:
In national income calculation, 'Inventory Investment' refers to the change in stock of goods that have been produced but not yet sold. It includes changes in stock of finished goods, semi-finished goods, and raw materials, as these are part of the production process and are ready for future sales. However, 'Change in sales during the year' is not included in inventory investment because it relates to goods already sold, not those held in stock. This is according to the 'Production Method' of national income calculation.

Extra Facts:
Inventory Investment is a key concept in Macroeconomics used for production and income calculation. It reflects changes in firms' stock levels. In GDP (Gross Domestic Product) calculation, inventory investment is considered part of investment expenditure. If stock increases, it is positive investment, and if it decreases, it is negative investment. It also indicates imbalance between production and demand in the economy.

question:
Which of the following is NOT one of the methods of national income estimation?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Banking method
Expenditure method
Product method
Income method
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Banking method

Explanation:
The three main methods of national income estimation are: Product method, Income method, and Expenditure method. The Product method sums up the value of all goods and services produced by all producers in the country. The Income method adds up all incomes earned by residents (wages, profits, rent, interest). The Expenditure method sums up all expenditures made by residents (consumption, investment, government spending, exports-imports). The Banking method is not a recognized method for national income estimation.

Extra Facts:
The methods of national income estimation are used to calculate GDP (Gross Domestic Product) and GNP (Gross National Product). GDP is the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year, while GNP includes income earned by citizens domestically and abroad. These methods are used to analyze economic growth rates, per capita income, and economic development.

☛ What is added in the Product method? → Value of goods and services

question:
It is possible to derive the value of GDP of a country. Which function of money is applicable here?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Store of value
Unit of account
Standard of deferred payments
Medium of exchange
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Unit of account

Explanation:
The 'Unit of account' function of money is applicable here because calculating Gross Domestic Product (GDP) requires expressing the value of various goods and services in a common unit (such as rupees, dollars, etc.). Money, through this function, helps measure and compare the values of different goods and services. It provides a standardized way to quantify economic activities, enabling the aggregation of diverse outputs into a single measurable figure like GDP.

Extra Facts:
Money has four primary functions: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, and standard of deferred payments. In GDP calculation, money is used to express values uniformly, allowing the assessment of an economy's overall performance. Without money, comparing the values of different goods and services or calculating aggregate indicators like GDP would be impossible. The unit of account function is foundational for economic measurement and analysis.

question:
In Economics, 'multiplier' is defined as the ratio of increase in income to increase in_______.

[RRC GROUP D]
options: liability
debt
credit
investment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is investment

Explanation:
In Economics, the 'multiplier' is defined as the ratio of increase in income to increase in investment. This concept is central to Keynesian economics, which states that an initial increase in investment can lead to a multiplied rise in income. The multiplier effect occurs when a portion of the income generated from investment is re-spent on consumption, creating further income and employment. The value of the multiplier depends on the MPC (Marginal Propensity to Consume), expressed by the formula k = 1/(1-MPC).

Extra Facts:
The multiplier effect highlights the importance of investment in an economy. It demonstrates how even small investments can generate large-scale economic activity. According to Keynes, government investment during recessions can stimulate recovery through this effect. The size of the multiplier also depends on the propensity to save - higher savings lead to a smaller multiplier effect.

☛ What is the range of Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC)? → Between 0 and 1
☛ At what point do savings equal investment? → Equilibrium Income Level
☛ What is the primary objective of Keynesian economics? → Solving economic depression
☛ How can national income be calculated? → Income, Output and Expenditure methods

अर्थशास्त्र में, 'गुणक' को आय में वृद्धि के निवेश में वृद्धि के अनुपात के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है। यह अवधारणा कीन्सियन अर्थशास्त्र में महत्वपूर्ण है, जो बताती है कि प्रारंभिक निवेश में वृद्धि से आय में कई गुना वृद्धि हो सकती है। गुणक प्रभाव तब होता है जब निवेश से उत्पन्न आय का एक हिस्सा पुनः खपत में जाता है, जिससे आगे आय और रोजगार सृजित होते हैं। गुणक का मूल्यांकन MPC (सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति) पर निर्भर करता है, जिसे सूत्र k = 1/(1-MPC) द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है।

Extra Facts:
गुणक प्रभाव अर्थव्यवस्था में निवेश के महत्व को उजागर करता है। यह दिखाता है कि छोटे निवेश से भी बड़े पैमाने पर आर्थिक गतिविधियाँ उत्पन्न हो सकती हैं। कीन्स के अनुसार, मंदी के दौर में सरकारी निवेश गुणक प्रभाव के माध्यम से आर्थिक सुधार ला सकता है। गुणक का आकार बचत की प्रवृत्ति पर भी निर्भर करता है - जितनी अधिक बचत, उतना कम गुणक प्रभाव।

question:
Which agency coordinates with various federal and state government agencies and departments to collect and compile the data required to calculate the GDP in India?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: National Statistical Office
Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Reserve Bank of India
Indian Statistical Institute
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Statistical Office

Explanation:
In India, the National Statistical Office (NSO) is responsible for collecting and compiling the data required to calculate GDP (Gross Domestic Product). NSO operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). This agency coordinates with various federal and state government agencies to gather data related to agriculture, industry, services, etc. The data released by NSO is used to compute key economic indicators such as national income, production, savings, and investment. NSO plays a crucial role in assisting the Government of India in formulating economic policies.

Extra Facts:
The National Statistical Office (NSO) was formed in 2019 by merging the Central Statistics Office (CSO) and the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO). The GDP data published by NSO is measured based on a base year, which is updated periodically. Currently, India calculates GDP using 2011-12 as the base year. NSO releases monthly, quarterly, and annual reports that reflect the progress of the economy.

question:
The value added of a firm is calculated as _________.

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: value of production of the firm - value of intermediate goods used by the firm
value of production of the firm + value of capital goods used by the firm
value of production of the firm ÷ value of intermediate goods used by the firm
value of production of the firm + value of intermediate goods used by the firm
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is value of production of the firm - value of intermediate goods used by the firm

Explanation:
Value Added represents the additional value created by a firm during the production process. It is calculated as the difference between the total value of production and the value of intermediate goods (like raw materials, energy, services) used in production. This concept is crucial in national income accounting as it measures the contribution of different sectors to the economy. The formula is: Gross Output – Intermediate Consumption. Value Added reflects the firm's real productivity and is also used in GDP calculation through the production approach.

Extra Facts:
Value Added can be categorized into: Gross Value Added (GVA), Net Value Added (NVA), and Value Added at Factor Cost. GVA includes depreciation, while NVA excludes it. Value Added at Factor Cost adjusts for indirect taxes and subsidies. This concept is pivotal in GDP calculation via the production method, where GDP is derived by summing up value added across all sectors.

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options_hi: फर्म के उत्पादन का मूल्य - फर्म द्वारा प्रयुक्त मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं का मूल्य

Explanation:
मूल्य आवर्धन (Value Added) एक फर्म द्वारा उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में जोड़े गए मूल्य को दर्शाता है। यह फर्म के कुल उत्पादन के मूल्य और उत्पादन में प्रयुक्त मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं (जैसे कच्चा माल, ऊर्जा, सेवाएं) के मूल्य के अंतर के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है। यह अवधारणा राष्ट्रीय आय लेखांकन में महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह अर्थव्यवस्था में विभिन्न क्षेत्रों द्वारा किए गए योगदान को मापती है। मूल्य आवर्धन की गणना कुल उत्पादन मूल्य - मध्यवर्ती उपभोग के रूप में की जाती है। यह फर्म की वास्तविक उत्पादकता को दर्शाता है और GDP की गणना में भी प्रयोग किया जाता है।

Extra Facts:
मूल्य आवर्धन तीन प्रकार का हो सकता है: सकल मूल्य आवर्धन (GVA), शुद्ध मूल्य आवर्धन (NVA), और कारक लागत पर मूल्य आवर्धन। GVA में मूल्यह्रास शामिल होता है, जबकि NVA में नहीं। कारक लागत पर मूल्य आवर्धन, अप्रत्यक्ष करों और सब्सिडी को समायोजित करता है। यह अवधारणा उत्पादन विधि द्वारा GDP की गणना में महत्वपूर्ण है, जहां सभी क्षेत्रों के मूल्य आवर्धन को जोड़कर GDP प्राप्त की जाती है।

question:
Which of the following is the INCORRECT sequence of national income from broader to narrower concepts?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: GNP at market prices - NNP at factor cost- NNP at market prices - GNP at factor cost
GNP at market prices - NNP at market prices - NNP at factor cost- Personal income
NNP at factor cost - Personal income - Personal disposable income
GNP at factor cost- NNP at factor cost- Personal income - Personal disposable income
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is GNP at market prices - NNP at factor cost- NNP at market prices - GNP at factor cost

Explanation:
The correct sequence of national income concepts from broader to narrower should be: GNP at market prices (GNPmp) → NNP at market prices (NNPmp) → NNP at factor cost (NNPfc) → Personal Income (PI) → Personal Disposable Income (PDI). In the given option, GNPmp is followed directly by NNPfc, which is incorrect because NNPmp should come first. Additionally, GNPfc appears at the end, which is not a narrower concept. This sequence is crucial in measuring national income and is useful in economic analysis.

Extra Facts:
In national income calculation, GNP (Gross National Product) and NNP (Net National Product) are key concepts. GNP includes depreciation, while NNP does not. Factor cost represents income paid to factors of production (labor, capital, land), whereas market price includes indirect taxes and subsidies. Personal Income and Disposable Income reflect the distribution and use of income at an individual level. These concepts help measure economic growth and development.

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा राष्ट्रीय आय का व्यापक से संकीर्ण अवधारणाओं का गलत क्रम है?

solution_hi:

Explanation:
राष्ट्रीय आय की अवधारणाओं का सही क्रम व्यापक से संकीर्ण होना चाहिए। सही क्रम है: बाजार मूल्य पर सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNPmp) → बाजार मूल्य पर निवल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (NNPmp) → कारक लागत पर निवल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (NNPfc) → वैयक्तिक आय (PI) → वैयक्तिक प्रयोज्य आय (PDI)। दिए गए विकल्प में, GNPmp के बाद सीधे NNPfc आता है, जो गलत है क्योंकि NNPmp पहले आना चाहिए। इसके अलावा, GNPfc अंत में आता है, जो कि संकीर्ण अवधारणा नहीं है। यह क्रम राष्ट्रीय आय के मापन में महत्वपूर्ण है और अर्थव्यवस्था के विश्लेषण में उपयोगी होता है।

Extra Facts:
राष्ट्रीय आय की गणना में GNP (सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद) और NNP (निवल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद) प्रमुख अवधारणाएँ हैं। GNP में मूल्यह्रास शामिल होता है, जबकि NNP में नहीं। कारक लागत पर आय उत्पादन के कारकों (श्रम, पूंजी, भूमि) को दिए गए पुरस्कार को दर्शाती है, जबकि बाजार मूल्य पर आय में अप्रत्यक्ष कर और सब्सिडी शामिल होती है। वैयक्तिक आय और प्रयोज्य आय व्यक्तिगत स्तर पर आय के वितरण और उपयोग को दर्शाती हैं। ये अवधारणाएँ अर्थव्यवस्था की वृद्धि और विकास को मापने में सहायक होती हैं।

question:
NDP at FC plus net factor income from abroad is equal to _______ .

NNP at FC
GDP at FC
GNP at MP
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is NNP at FC

NDP (Net Domestic Product) at FC (Factor Cost) represents the net value of goods and services produced within a country's borders after deducting depreciation. solution:

- GNP (सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद) देश के नागरिकों द्वारा देश के अंदर और बाहर किए गए उत्पादन को मापता है, जबकि GDP केवल देश की सीमाओं के भीतर उत्पादन को मापता है।
- NNP (निवल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद) = GNP - मूल्यह्रास।
- GDP में केवल अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं को शामिल किया जाता है, मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं को नहीं, ताकि दोहरी गणना (Double Counting) से बचा जा सके।
